ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $y=kx+b$ ($k\neq 0$) intersects the x-axis at point $A(6,0)$ and the y-axis at point $B(0,3)$, and intersects the line $y=x$ at point $C$. Find the values of $k$ and $b$, and the coordinates of point $C$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given the line $y=kx+b$ ($k\neq 0$) intersects the x-axis at point A(6, 0) and the y-axis at point B(0, 3),\\
$\therefore \left\{\begin{array}{l}
6k+b=0\\ 
b=3
\end{array}\right.$\\
Solving this system, we get: $\left\{\begin{array}{l}
k=-\frac{1}{2}\\ 
b=3
\end{array}\right.$,\\
Hence, the equation of line $AB$ is: $y=-\frac{1}{2}x+3$,\\
By solving the system: $\left\{\begin{array}{l}
y=-\frac{1}{2}x+3\\ 
y=x
\end{array}\right.$,\\
We find: $\left\{\begin{array}{l}
x=2\\ 
y=2
\end{array}\right.$,\\
Therefore, $C(2, 2).$\\
$\therefore k=\boxed{-\frac{1}{2}}, b=\boxed{3}, \boxed{C\left(2, 2\right)}.$
